title: Draft value hypotheses without copying outcomes
nav: 3. Draft value hypotheses without copying outcomes
objective: Repair an AI statement: 'this customer saved 40% because a peer did'.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: AI drafting tools sometimes pull in other customers' outcomes. A peer's result is not evidence about the prospect.
Build from the customer's own evidence

Use the customer's strategy, meeting notes, and stated priorities to draft strategic priorities, risks, and proposed Positive Business Outcomes. A safe draft is labeled "hypothesis to validate" and links to the customer evidence it is based on. Glean's Value Playbook warns against the failure where teams present benchmarks as proof.
Peer examples are analogies at most
A peer example can be used as an analogy only when it is approved for that use. Keep a possible support-efficiency opportunity for this prospect separate from a proven outcome at another company.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Never turn another customer's success into the prospect's own result. Remove uncleared names, figures, and confidential details before sharing with partners or customers.
Another customer's result is an analogy at most. The hypothesis has to be built from this customer's evidence.

blocks.title: Copied outcome versus grounded hypothesis
blocks.alt: A comparison of a copied outcome, which reuses a peer's result as a promise, with a grounded hypothesis, which uses the customer's own volumes and times, states assumptions, and labels evidence.

items.b: Uses this customer's volumes and times
